_readme: The allowance window, agreed across THREE implementations (ss#2618).
src/lib/admin/medchron-jobs-read.ts (console), and the laptop pipeline in the
private engagements repo (tools/medchron/limits.py), which vendors a COPY of
this file and pins its sha256 the way tests/customer-yaml-parity-contract.ts
Expectations here are HAND-AUTHORED from Stripe's documented anchor rule, not
generated from any implementation. A table generated from the code it checks
proves only that the code equals itself.
TAGGED VALUES: a settings value of the form {"__float__": N} means the
native float N, not an object. JSON has one number type; YAML has two, and
the int/float distinction is exactly what one reader accepts and another
refuses. Each side must materialise the tag before calling its reader.

reader.why: no cycle authored -> calendar month, not an error
a quoted number is the divergence this table exists for: it validates against the open scalar map and projects to D1 as a string

a float is not a day of the month — and the two languages CANNOT agree here. YAML 15.0 is a float in Python (refused) and is indistinguishable from 15 in JS (accepted). That asymmetry is irreducible, so it is declared rather than papered over: the SEAT is the authority and refuses, so no job runs; the console may render a window the seat will not honour, which is what its drift notice is for
bool is an int in Python; true is not a day
authored null is authored-but-unreadable, not absent

window.why: no anchor -> the calendar month, which is today's behaviour and what an unauthored seat keeps
before the anchor day -> the window that began last month
window.label: the cycle ending Sep 14

window.why: exactly on the boundary: the anchor instant belongs to the NEW cycle (half-open)
window.label: the cycle ending Oct 14

window.why: STRIPE RETURN-TO-ANCHOR, step 1: a 31st anchor in a 28-day month clamps
window.label: the cycle ending Feb 27

window.why: STRIPE RETURN-TO-ANCHOR, step 2: and then RETURNS to the 31st. Chaining from the previous end would give Mar 28 here, which is the classic wrong answer this vector exists to catch
window.label: the cycle ending Mar 30

window.why: leap year: a 30th anchor clamps to Feb 29, not Feb 28
window.label: the cycle ending Feb 28

window.why: PHOENIX BOUNDARY. The firm is UTC-7. A job created 2026-09-14 at 23:00 local is 2026-09-15T06:00Z, so it lands in the NEW cycle though it is still the 14th where the firm sits. The cycle turns at UTC midnight; this vector pins that we chose it deliberately
window.label: the cycle ending Oct 14

window.why: effective_from truncates the FIRST cycle so no already-debited row is re-partitioned into it
window.label: the cycle ending Oct 14

window.why: effective_from in the past is inert once the first cycle has passed
window.label: the cycle ending Dec 14
